summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of T1-T2 paraplegia, recurrent pneumonias, neurogenic bladder, and restrictive ventilatory defect on home oxygen was admitted with fever, increased secretions, and dyspnea. She had a history of recent hospitalization for pneumonia and septic shock. Imaging showed a right pleural effusion and right lower lobe opacity, concerning for aspiration pneumonia. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, but developed leukopenia and thrombocytopenia, prompting a switch from cefepime and vancomycin to ceftaroline. A repeat chest X-ray revealed new mild pulmonary edema, suggesting acute diastolic heart failure. Despite medical recommendations to remain hospitalized, she elected to leave against medical advice. She was discharged home with services on IV antibiotics (ceftaroline and flagyl) via home infusion, oral lasix, and all baseline medications, with instructions to follow up in primary care, pulmonary, and infectious disease clinics.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomitus
